# Populated Gophish migration corpus

`rich.sql` is a synthetic dataset authored against the Gophish 0.12.1 models and original migrations at commit `95618469799295e2c0fec980805a2dfbb818816b`. It is not a captured production database or a claim that these rows were generated through the Go API. SQLite tests copy the independent `../gophish-v0.12.1/legacy-latest.sqlite3` snapshot; MySQL tests replay the unmodified `../mysql-legacy/` scripts. Both apply the same data before opening the real Ruphish provider. The account hash is supplied from the independently Go-captured `password.json` fixture.

The corpus covers accounts and roles, account locks and password-reset flags, owner isolation, overlapping groups, empty groups, recipient snapshots that differ from current targets, Unicode, mixed and plain-only templates, binary and empty attachments, custom headers, SMTP credentials, deleted campaign resources, active/completed/queued campaigns, recipient statuses, repeated events, sensitive legacy event details and locations, pending/in-flight/completed/blocked mail, mailbox defaults and credentials, global webhooks, and test-email records. Dates and domains are synthetic; provider tests do not run external workers.

`crates/ruphish-adapters/tests/support/legacy_migration.rs` owns explicit expected public outcomes and storage checks. The same assertions run immediately after conversion and after reopening. Its queue mutations isolate negative/overflow retries, missing dates or recipients, wrong owners or campaigns, duplicate queue rows, and globally colliding tracking IDs. Each case must retain the exact unresolved queue identities and exclude them from runnable deliveries.

Separate regressions cover deleted-ID counters (including empty tables and interrupted MySQL publication), IMAP rows left by Gophish account deletion and malformed owner IDs (skipped while valid data imports, with originals retained only in recovery data), and historical status/date/role transformations. SQLite rollback coverage rejects missing required campaign owners instead of coercing them to identity zero. The existing 25-version SQLite and 28-version MySQL sweeps remain in place. This corpus adds data variety without multiplying every scenario across every historical schema.
